description: New north star for Helping Hands: this video — https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=itGeItWc2rw — 'Can this VLA Work with no Dataset? I Put MolmoAct2 to Test'. Jake says this is the direction. Watch/read up on it: MolmoAct2 and vision-language-action models doing real manipulation with no task-specific dataset, zero-shot from a camera and a natural-language instruction. Work out what it means for Helping Hands — what the app's job becomes if a VLA does the perception and action planning, what we capture and send, what UI and hardware assumptions change, and what concretely should change in this codebase. Do the digging yourself and report back with findings and a recommendation before writing code.

results.identified_issue: Research/recommendation item, no product code by request. Grounding: arXiv 2605.02881 (paper), https://huggingface.co/docs/lerobot/main/en/molmoact2 (the practically useful source — has the hardware lerobot-rollout section, camera key names cam0/cam1, and the joint_signs/joint_offsets correction). Paper's own limitations section says zero-shot is brittle and below deployable thresholds; SO-100/101 zero-shot OOD = 56.7% vs DROID/Franka 87.1%. The SO100_101 checkpoint is fine-tuned on filtered community data, so the video's 'no dataset' framing is about task-specific data, not pretraining data — I called that out because getting it wrong would set expectations far too high. Repo facts verified by reading: record_actions.sh captures only the six JOINT_KEYS at 20Hz, no camera; grep for camera/opencv/AVCapture across the repo hits only CAD render scripts and SceneKit; no URLSession anywhere under HelpingHands/, so the app has zero robot I/O today; Scripts/lehome_sim_bootstrap.sh and plans/lehome_pillowcase.md already document the no-Mac/NVIDIA wall. Did NOT verify: the video's actual content (WebFetch on YouTube returns no transcript or description), and nothing was run on hardware. Alternatives rejected: rewriting the app around a task-instruction UI now (premature — no evidence the policy works on our rig yet), and vendoring weights/code (the existing doc's no-vendoring stance is right). If this turns out wrong, the most likely reason is that the video demonstrates a workflow or checkpoint I didn't find.
results.summary: Dug into MolmoAct2 and wrote up what a VLA changes for Helping Hands — the answer to the video's question is 'not yet, but the demo-recording step mostly goes away.'
results.detailed_description:
I read the MolmoAct2 paper and Ai2's LeRobot deployment docs and wrote the findings into plans/molmoact2.md, so you can listen to it in the app. Two things worth knowing up front. Ai2's own number for zero-shot on our exact arms is 56.7% success, and the paper calls zero-shot "brittle." And "no dataset" means no dataset for YOUR task — the SO-100/101 checkpoint is still fine-tuned, just on community data we didn't have to record. That's still the real win: 50-200 demos per task stops being the price of admission.

Three things block us. We have no cameras at all — record_actions.sh saves six joint floats and nothing else, and training_pipeline.md literally says "start position-only, add vision later." That has to invert. We have no NVIDIA GPU and there's no Apple Silicon path, same wall as the LeHome work. And the SO-101 checkpoint needs a joint-sign correction or the arm drives backwards; the LeRobot-converted checkpoint has it baked in, the raw allenai one doesn't.

My recommendation is cheapest-test-first: two USB webcams (one scene, one wrist), rent a Linux GPU box, then run one lerobot-rollout command with a spoken task string and score it on pick-and-place. Don't touch the app until that produces a number — except a stop button, which is safety, not a bet.

I could not get a transcript of the video, so I answered its title question from the paper. If the creator found something different, tell me and I'll redo the top of that doc. I also flagged one tension for you to call: the iBackpack video-to-servo learning pipeline is basically building a VLA from scratch, and MolmoAct2 may make that half redundant.
